summary: Piotr Klafkowski is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatsho, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Tulku Jampa Kelsang Rinpoche.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka worked in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate at Leiden University under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He founded Udayana University and held professorships there, at Gadjah Mada University, and at the University of Indonesia.

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis, and became a clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont in 1994.
Pori Park is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. She has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.
Poulami Ray is a history and archaeology researcher who studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen. Ray is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who taught Kuntala Bhattacharya. He held posts at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture and as a professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 2009).
Prabhasa Dharma was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies. She undertook traditional training under teachers Kyozan Joshu Sasaki and Seikaku Hirata.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi. He held professorships at the University of Calcutta, Peking University, and Visva-Bharati University.

Prafulla Chandra Ray was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Vidyasagar College, University of Calcutta, and University of Edinburgh. He held professorial posts at Presidency University, University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture, and University of Calcutta.
Pragati Sahni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Damien Keown. She serves as an associate professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).
Praggnaparamita Biswas is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Ratna Basu. She is attested as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Prahlad Pradhan was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Patna University and Visva-Bharati University. His career included serving as a professor at Utkal University and principal at Gangadhar Meher University.

Pramod Chandra was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Mumbai. He served as a professor at the University of Chicago and later as a professor at Harvard University from 1980 to 2004.
Prasarn Lao-areun is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Viroj Inthanon and earned a PhD from the University of Mysore (attested 2014).
Pratap Chandra Chunder was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.

Pratapaditya Pal is a scholar of art history, Indology, and Tibetology who earned doctorates from the University of Calcutta and Cambridge. He held curatorial posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

id: P:Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark
summary: Prince Peter of Greece and Denmark was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly and the London School of Economics, and served with the Office of Strategic Services.

Priyanku Chakraborty is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral research under Aishwarya Biswas. In 2026, Chakraborty is attested as the Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at The Asiatic Society.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø is an Iranian, Central Asian, linguistics, and Indology scholar educated at Oslo and Mainz. He taught at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and served as Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies at Harvard University from circa 1991 to 2015.
